1.explanation:
1. We import the Carbon React components (Form, TileGroup, RadioTile, Button) and their CSS.  
2. We wrap three <RadioTile> inputs in a <TileGroup> inside a native HTML <form>.  
3. Each RadioTile has the required attribute so that on submit, the browser’s native form validation is triggered if none are selected.  
4. Because Carbon renders the actual radio <input> off-screen (opacity: 0; position: absolute), the browser places its validation bubble where that input lives in the DOM (typically top-left of the tile group).  
5. Submitting without picking a tile shows the bubble at the wrong spot, reproducing the bug exactly as in the screenshots.
1.bug_scenario: When you place a set of RadioTile components (wrapped in a TileGroup) inside a native HTML form and mark them as required, the browser’s built-in validation will fire on submit and display its warning bubble—but because the actual <input type="radio"> elements are positioned off-screen (invisibly), the validation bubble appears at an odd place (usually the top-left of the group) rather than centered under the tile or at the bottom of the group.
